sum: Investing.com -- Merck KGaA shares climbed to a 52-week high on Thursday after the German healthcare and technology group beat analyst expectations for third-quarter revenue and adjusted earnings, while raising its full-year guidance on stronger demand across its life science and electronics businesses.
Shares rose 2.1% to €154.85, outperforming Germany's benchmark DAX, which gained around 0.7% during the session.

Merck reported third-quarter net sales of €5.63 billion, up 5.8% from a year earlier. However, operating profit (EBIT) fell 46.5% to €653 million, while net profit declined 49.9% to €450 million, reflecting a high comparison base after several one-off benefits in the year-earlier quarter.
EBITDA fell 3.8% to €1.62 billion, while the company's preferred adjusted measure, EBITDA pre, increased 0.8% to €1.68 billion. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS pre) remained unchanged at €2.32.
According to Jefferies, quarterly revenue beat consensus by 3.1%, while EBITDA pre exceeded expectations by 4.7%. Earnings per share also came in above the €2.20 consensus estimate.

Life Science revenue grew 6.1% organically, led by Process Solutions, where demand for biopharmaceutical manufacturing materials remained strong. Electronics revenue increased 13.3%, supported by a 18.7% rise in Semiconductor Solutions sales as demand for advanced chipmaking materials accelerated alongside AI-related investment. Healthcare also benefited from 41.5% growth in Rare Diseases, although generic competition drove a 25.1% decline in Mavenclad sales.

The company raised its 2026 net sales forecast to €21.5 billion-€21.9 billion, from €21 billion-€21.8 billion previously. EBITDA pre guidance was increased to €6.2 billion-€6.4 billion from €5.9 billion-€6.3 billion, while EPS pre guidance was lifted to €8.30-€8.70.

MRK's 2027 Outlook Challenging, Long-Term Prospects Promising
sum: Merck MRK announced strong third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 29, with both adjusted earnings and revenues surpassing estimates. Third-quarter 2026 sales were $18.1 billion, up 5% year over year, while adjusted earnings declined 3% to $2.49 per share. Keytruda/Keytruda Qlex sales rose 6% to $8.6 billion. Merck raised its 2026 guidance, projecting revenues of $66.8-$67.3 billion and adjusted EPS of $2.77-$2.82
On the call, Merck also provided a preliminary outlook for 2027 and shed light on its long-term growth outlook.

Merck expects moderate revenue growth in 2027 as contributions from new product launches and higher sales in Animal Health are expected to be partially offset by generic headwinds. Merck expects more than $2 billion of generic headwinds due to loss of exclusivity of drugs like Bridion, the Januvia family of products, as well as Adempas. Keytruda is expected to remain a significant revenue contributor, although sales growth will likely moderate as the drug approaches peak penetration across several approved indications. Pricing pressures in international markets, particularly Germany, could also weigh on Keytruda’s sales.

Merck also expects challenges in its vaccines business, mainly for the HPV vaccine, Gardasil, due to increased vaccine hesitancy and declining utilization. Additionally, an approximately $250 million benefit from CDC vaccine purchases in 2026 is expected to reverse in 2027.

On the profitability front, gross margins are expected to improve following the expiration of a royalty obligation associated with Keytruda. However, underlying operating expenses are expected to rise at a mid-to-high single-digit rate, reflecting investments in its expanding pipeline and growing portfolio of new product launches.

Keytruda’s core U.S. patent is expected to expire around 2028, with additional patents expiring slightly after that. Keytruda is expected to face significant biosimilar competition around 2028-2029. Once biosimilars enter, Keytruda’s sales are likely to decline sharply. Merck expects a shallow dip in total revenues and earnings in the initial period following Keytruda LOE before quickly returning to growth.

sum: Lonza agreed on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, to acquire five contract development and manufacturing organization sites in the United States from Merck KGaA. The Lonza announcement puts the enterprise valuation in the low- to mid-triple-digit millions of Swiss francs and expects the transaction to close in mid-2027, subject to customary closing conditions.

The acquisition will increase Lonza's US CDMO network from four to nine sites and add approximately 1,100 employees. Lonza said its US workforce will rise to more than 6,000 people. Until closing, the acquired businesses will continue to operate independently within Merck KGaA.

The sites add capabilities from clinical development through commercial manufacturing. The St. Louis, Missouri, operation specializes in bioconjugates, while facilities in Madison and Verona, Wisconsin, produce high-potency payload-linkers used in antibody-drug conjugates.

A Carlsbad, California, site provides end-to-end viral-vector services, including aseptic fill-finish. The Indianapolis, Indiana, operation covers lipid nanoparticles, liposomes and PEGylated proteins, also with aseptic fill-finish capabilities. Together, the sites broaden Lonza's offering in bioconjugates, cell and gene therapy and advanced drug delivery.

Lonza expects the acquired sites to generate around CHF 250 million in sales in full-year 2028. Their CORE EBITDA margin is expected to remain below Lonza's group margin initially, with an insignificant impact on the group. The company said the businesses could reach Lonza's future group margin level at peak sales by the middle of the 2030s.

The consideration will be paid in cash using cash on hand and existing credit facilities, according to Lonza. The company said the funding structure maintains its BBB+ rating and does not affect the previously announced share buyback after the expected year-end 2026 closing of the Capsules & Health Ingredients divestment.

Chief Executive Wolfgang Wienand described the transaction as a fit with Lonza's One Lonza strategy and said it should bring the company closer to US customers while increasing the resilience of its manufacturing network.

Merck Recommends Rejection of TRC Capital’s “Mini-Tender” Offer
sum: RAHWAY, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Merck (NYSE: MRK), known as MSD outside the United States and Canada, has been notified that TRC Capital Investment Corporation (TRC Capital) has commenced an unsolicited “mini-tender” offer, dated November 12, 2024, to purchase up to 1,000,000 shares of Merck common stock at $96.38 per share. The offer price is approximately 4.32% below the closing price of the Merck common stock on November 11, 2024 ($100.73), the last trading day before the date of the offer, and approximately 3.48% below the closing price of the Merck common stock on November 21, 2024 ($99.86), the day prior to this release.

Merck does not endorse TRC Capital’s offer and recommends that Merck shareholders reject the offer and not tender their shares in response to TRC Capital’s unsolicited mini-tender offer. This mini-tender offer is at a price below the closing price for Merck’s shares (as of the day prior to this release) and is subject to numerous conditions, including TRC Capital’s ability to obtain financing. Merck is not associated in any way with TRC Capital, its mini-tender offer or the offer documentation.

TRC Capital has made similar unsolicited mini-tender offers for shares of other publicly traded companies. Mini-tender offers seek to acquire less than 5% of a company's outstanding shares. This lets the offering company avoid many of the disclosure and procedural requirements the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) requires for tender offers. As a result, mini-tender offers do not provide investors the same level of protections as provided by larger tender offers under U.S. federal securities laws.

On its website, the SEC advises that the people behind mini tender-offers “frequently use mini-tender offers to catch shareholders off guard” and that investors “may end up selling at below-market prices.” The SEC's website also contains important tips for investors regarding mini-tender offers.
Like TRC Capital’s other offers, this one puts individual investors at risk because they may not realize they are selling their shares at a discount.

Is Merck (NYSE:MRK) Stock A Bargain Despite Its Strong Rally?
sum: A pharmaceutical giant posts fresh oncology wins after a strong multiyear run, as a cash flow model suggests the stock still trades well below its intrinsic value.

Few areas of medicine have changed as dramatically in recent years as cancer treatment, and Merck & Co., Inc. A member of the S&P 500, the pharmaceutical giant has delivered a strong multiyear run, and fresh oncology data keeps adding to its momentum. New results in endometrial cancer and expanded treatment options in bladder cancer strengthen its pipeline. A discounted cash flow model suggests the stock still trades well below its intrinsic value. The question is whether the market has fully priced in the durability of Merck's cancer franchise.

Merck is a global healthcare company that discovers, develops, and produces prescription medicines, vaccines, biologic therapies, and animal health products. Its flagship cancer immunotherapy, KEYTRUDA, ranks among the most widely used treatments in oncology. The company also produces vaccines that protect against infectious diseases. As a leading healthcare stock, Merck operates research and manufacturing facilities worldwide, serving patients, physicians, and veterinarians across many countries.

Merck's stock has delivered a strong return over the past several years, rewarding long-term owners as its oncology franchise expanded. A run of that size places significant expectations into the stock price, which makes the link to future cash generation especially important. For a large pharmaceutical company, value depends heavily on how long its key medicines can generate cash and how successfully new therapies replace older ones.

Merck has also expanded treatment options in bladder cancer, giving physicians more tools to treat patients with this challenging disease. Expanding into additional cancer types and treatment settings extends the reach of Merck's oncology portfolio. Each new approval can broaden the patient population served by its medicines, supporting revenue growth and strengthening the company's position as a leader in cancer care.

A company that keeps three-quarters of its revenue as gross profit does not lose money at the operating line by selling medicine. Merck is spending its way out of a problem that arrives later this decade, when its largest product loses protection. The income statement is the cost of that attempt, booked all at once.

Merck booked an acquired research charge of roughly $9.00 billion against the Cidara acquisition in the first quarter, and a further charge for Terns in the second. Accounting rules send that straight through research and development expense rather than onto the balance sheet. Neither charge carried a tax benefit, which is why the damage reaches the bottom line undiluted and why an operating margin reads below zero.

The cash statement shows what actually happened. An acquired research charge is a purchase price written off at once rather than money walking out the door each quarter, and free cash flow came in at several times reported net income. That also explains the payout ratio, because the dividend costs 266.67% of earnings and a small fraction of the cash. A charge that never cost a dollar is exactly the distortion that makes reported payout ratios useless across the pharmaceutical dividend payers we ranked for 2026, where the name we put first is up 13% since.
The underlying business did not shrink while this happened. Revenue grew 5.10% in the most recent quarter.

sum: Shares of Moderna MRNA) and Merck MRK) are soaring Wednesday after the companies reported a potentially historic breakthrough for their personalized mRNA cancer vaccine, intismeran autogene (V940/mRNA-4157), in combination with Merck's blockbuster immunotherapy Keytruda.

The Phase 3 INTerpath-001 study met its primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival and a key secondary endpoint of distant metastasis-free survival in patients with completely resected stage IIB-IV melanoma skin cancer.

The companies said the improvements versus Keytruda alone were both statistically significant and clinically meaningful. Importantly, this represents the first positive Phase 3 readout for an individualized neoantigen therapy and an mRNA-based cancer therapy.

Investors have responded accordingly. Moderna shares have more than doubled intraday, while Merck stock has jumped over 10%. The question is whether investors should chase either stock after today's enormous move.

Moderna's intismeran is individually manufactured using mutations identified from each patient's tumor and can encode up to 34 neoantigens intended to teach the immune system to recognize cancer cells. It is then paired with Merck's Keytruda, which helps remove mechanisms cancer cells use to evade an immune response.

The Phase 3 success also validates encouraging earlier results. Five-year Phase 2b data showed that intismeran plus Keytruda reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 49% and the risk of distant metastasis or death by 59% compared with Keytruda alone.

That said, the companies have not yet disclosed the detailed Phase 3 efficacy numbers, making the eventual medical-conference presentation an important catalyst. They intend to discuss potential regulatory submissions with authorities. Meanwhile, the broader INTerpath program includes nine Phase 2 and Phase 3 trials across cancers including melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer, bladder cancer, and renal cell carcinoma.

sum: On June 25, 2026, Merck KGaA announced its intention to acquire American biotechnology company Bio-Techne Corp for $11.3 billion, a move that would expand its position in the life sciences market.
Following this, Bio-Techne’s shares rose 22% in premarket trading, and Merck’s offer of $73 per share implies roughly a 24% premium to Bio-Techne’s close on Wednesday.

Under the deal, Merck will gain access to Bio-Techne’s research expertise and supplies for scientific development, including reagents, proteins, antibodies, and other tools used by scientists and drug developers.

But while the market was focused on the rearview mirror, management was busy talking about the next twenty cars in the garage. And they weren’t being subtle about it.

When Merck unveiled its $6.7 billion buyout bid for Terns Pharmaceuticals last month, analysts called the deal a bargain for the pharma. Now, new disclosures about the drug at the center of the acquisition have dampened that enthusiasm and revealed that Merck had once offered roughly $1 billion more.

“The emergence of a higher bidder is unlikely,” William Blair told investors in a note on Tuesday, walking back its previous assessment of the acquisition. “We now believe that the Merck acquisition will be completed later this quarter.” Merck initiated its tender offer for Terns on the same day.

The pharma had initially proposed to purchase Terns’ shares for $61 a pop, according to an SEC filing posted on Tuesday, resulting in a total offer of around $7.7 billion. This was in early February, at which point Terns was also fielding an acquisition offer from an unnamed “large pharmaceutical company,” which had proposed a per-share price of $58—an offer that it later raised to $61.

Days after Merck’s initial proposal, Terns provided both of its suitors with updated clinical data from the Phase 1 CARDINAL study of TERN-701, an oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor being tested for chronic myeloid leukemia and the biotech’s lead asset.

Tuesday’s SEC document did not detail what these updated findings were, revealing only that “the MMR [major molecular response] achievement rate was lower” than the 64% rate at 24 weeks that had previously been disclosed in a December 2025 presentation. MMR is a common bellwether for how effective a leukemia therapy is.

Merck seemed underwhelmed by these new disclosures and lowered its proposed purchase price to $50 per share. “Merck believed that the MMR achievement rate for TERN-701 would likely be at the low end of the range discussed by Terns management,” the biotech reported in its securities filing.

A giant in the healthcare space, Merck (NYSE:MRK) shares are up 13.5% year-to-date and trading near $119.47, yet retail sentiment on Reddit has slipped from a bullish 63 over the past quarter to a neutral 43 this week. The catalyst is Merck's February 23 announcement to split its Human Health business into two divisions: one focused on oncology, the other on specialty pharma and infectious diseases. Investors are asking whether this restructuring is a confident pivot or a quiet acknowledgment that the Keytruda era is ending.

Keytruda, the world's top-selling drug, accounts for roughly half of Merck's revenue (49%), and its compound patent expires in December 2028. CEO Robert M. Davis stated on the Q4 earnings call that "we now have line of sight to over $70 billion of potential commercial opportunity by the mid-2030s, $20 billion more than just a year ago and more than double consensus 2028 peak KEYTRUDA revenue." RBC Capital initiated coverage with an Outperform rating and a $142 price target, arguing that the company will return to growth in the early 2030s sooner than the market assumes. The consensus 12-month price target sits at $123 with 6 Buy and 6 Hold ratings and no Strong Buy calls, suggesting measured confidence rather than conviction.

sum: In light of the recent meltdown of most of the market's top technology names, are boring ol' dividend stocks suddenly much more attractive? For plenty of investors this now seems to be the case.

And if you're going to start your search for greener pastures anywhere in particular, the blue chip names of the Dow Jones Industrial Average may be a great place to begin -- and even end -- the effort.

If you're looking for just above-average price appreciation, forget it -- Verizon Communications (VZ +0.81%) can't offer it. The United States' mobile phone market is highly saturated, and highly competitive. Last quarter's year-over-year revenue growth of about 2% is about as good as it gets. This ticker's dividend, however, makes these slow-moving capital gains worth it. Newcomers will be plugging into this name while its forward-looking yield stands at 6.1%, which would be difficult to match with any other name that brings a comparable risk to the table.

The business itself is, of course, well-suited for supporting recurring dividend payments. Consumers may postpone the purchase of a new car or skip a vacation. But they're not about to give up the device in their pocket or purse that keeps them connected to the rest of the world.

It would be naïve to pretend pharmaceutical giant Merck (MRK +1.38%) didn't become a little too dependent on its cancer-fighting Keytruda (which now accounts for roughly half of its sales) knowing it was headed toward patent expiration beginning in 2028. It would also be disingenuous, however, to ignore the fact that the company's been taking enormous strides in preparation for that day.
